hints.title: Reverse Ancestor Traversal
hints.text: If an edge connects u to v, then u is an ancestor of v. Traversing forward from each node u reaches all nodes for which u is an ancestor.

hints.title: Natural Sorted Order
hints.text: Run depth-first search starting from node 0 up to n - 1. When visiting descendant v from source u, add u to v's ancestor list.

hints.title: Visited Pruning
hints.text: Maintain a visited array for each source search to ensure each node is explored at most once per root.

hints.title: Complete Python Solution

complexity.time: O(V * (V + E)) depth-first search from each node
complexity.notes: Forward reachability from sorted source nodes.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Collecting ancestors backwards without sorting requires repeated set sorting across all nodes.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Traversing in ascending source order builds strictly sorted ancestor lists with zero post-sort overhead.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Traverse from sources in sorted order to avoid final O(N log N) sorting per node.

solutions.approach: Python forward DFS in ascending node order.
C++ forward DFS in increasing source order.
Java recursive DFS from ascending roots.
JavaScript DFS traversal in ascending root order.
